title: Renalysis of PXD059683, SpLICE: A reference database enabling in depth proteome and PTM analysis of mouse immune cells
projectDescription: Renalyzing the PXD059683, SpLICE: A reference database enabling in depth proteome and PTM analysis of mouse immune cells consisting of B Cell, T Cell, Dendritic Cell, Cell Culture, Macrophage data which is available at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/archive/projects/PXD059683 using MaxQuant v 2.7.0.0.
sampleProcessingProtocol: This is a reanalysis of data in PRIDE project ID PXD059683, SpLICE: A reference database enabling in depth proteome and PTM analysis of mouse immune cells.
dataProcessingProtocol: MaxQuant v 2.7.0.0 (Ref:MaxQuant enables high peptide identification rates, individualized p.p.b.-range mass accuracies and proteome-wide protein quantification | Nature Biotechnology) is used to reprocess the PXD059683 (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/archive/projects/PXD059683).  Along with defaults, deamidation of asparagine/glutamine, methylation of Lysine and Arginine, and phosphorylation of Serine, Threonine and Tryptophan as dynamic post-translational modification was appended following the data-processing protocol in original data https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/archive/projects/PXD059683. Search performed against the Mouse proteome including isoforms downloaded from Uniprot (https://www.uniprot.org) in August 2025 along with MaxQuant’s internal contaminants database using Andromeda built into MaxQuant. Match-between-runs (MBR) functionality is utilized to reduce missing values in raw data. MBR verifies the presence of a peptide signal in one sample that wasn’t identified in another. This is achieved by utilizing high mass precision and a restricted retention time period of 1-minute with 20-minutes overall sliding window. If this particular signal is detected, it is labeled as ‘By matching’ instead of ‘By MS/MS’ in the output. Both protein and peptide group identifications false discovery rate was kept at 1% and only unique peptides with high confidence were used for final protein group identification. Intensity values for each protein-group were normalized using label-free quantification (LFQ) algorithm  (Ref:Accurate Proteome-wide Label-free Quantification by Delayed Normalization and Maximal Peptide Ratio Extraction, Termed MaxLFQ - ScienceDirect) with at least 1 unique peptide.
